assumptions: hbar is strictly positive; numerical diagnostics set hbar=1
the weighted measure, left-weighted ordering, C_c^infinity core, and full Lebesgue-p Fourier base are declared quantization inputs rather than consequences of classical C
the sign-reversed fiber expression is put in the standard real Sturm-Liouville form with leading coefficient 2*hbar^2, weight f>0, and locally integrable potential
Weyl endpoint type is independent of the nonreal spectral parameter once the declared Sturm-Liouville hypotheses hold
the zero-energy modified-Bessel solutions may therefore be used to classify endpoint type, but they do not themselves construct the nonreal deficiency vectors
a fiberwise U(1) extension statement is not promoted to the classification of all full-operator extensions
a Borel theta(p) is necessary but not by itself sufficient for a p-preserving decomposable extension; a measurable field of boundary maps, domains or resolvents must also be supplied
the p=0 fiber is audited separately but has Lebesgue measure zero unless an extra origin atom is declared

candidate_raw_C_operator_domain_family.conditional_p_preserving_recipe: requires Borel theta(p) and a separately verified measurable field of boundary maps, domains or resolvents
candidate_raw_C_operator_domain_family.fiber_deficiency_indices: n_plus=n_minus=1 for every fixed p under theorem guards
candidate_raw_C_operator_domain_family.fixed_p_extensions: one real projective, equivalently U(1), boundary line per fixed p
candidate_raw_C_operator_domain_family.minimal_operator: C_min=f^(-1)*H_hat on C_c^infinity in L2(f dQ dphi)

declared_candidate.extension_scope: fixed-p self-adjoint extensions plus a conditional recipe for decomposable extensions that preserve p; no measurable global domain or resolvent field is claimed
declared_candidate.fourier_base: Lebesgue p in R, with -i*hbar*d_phi mapped to p
declared_candidate.no_selected_extension: theta(p), any parity restriction, and any p-fiber mixing are not supplied by the classical rescaling
declared_candidate.weighted_auxiliary_space: H_C=L2(R_Q times R_phi, f(Q) dQ dphi)

Q_minus_infinity.actual_boundary_maps: Wronskian limits against a real zero-energy pair c_p,s_p normalized at Q_0=0

endpoint_classification.fiber_deficiency_indices: n_plus=n_minus=1 for every fixed p under the declared Weyl guards

fiber_extension_and_direct_integral_boun.actual_fiber_condition: one real projective line in Wronskian boundary maps Gamma_0,p and Gamma_1,p
fiber_extension_and_direct_integral_boun.measurability_requirement: Borel theta(p) plus a measurable field of boundary maps, domains or resolvents, up to almost-everywhere equality
fiber_extension_and_direct_integral_boun.p_zero_full_base_role: Lebesgue-null unless a separate p=0 atom is declared

exact_checks.statement: the frozen positive multiplier f=12*pi^2*exp(3Q/2) gives H=f*C exactly
U chi=f^(1/2) chi and U^(-1) psi=g psi are inverse isometries between L2(f dQ dphi) and flat L2 and preserve C_c^infinity
the f weight cancels f^(-1), and integration by parts leaves only the 2*hbar^2 Q-Wronskian and -3*hbar^2 phi-Wronskian, both zero on the compact core
U*C_min*U^(-1)=g*H_hat*g has the exact expanded flat differential expression including the -3*hbar^2*d_Q and 9*hbar^2/8 terms
on Fourier plane waves the formal raw fiber symbol is C_p=f^(-1)[2*hbar^2*d_Q^2+3*p^2-72*pi^4*exp(2Q)]; the operator direct integral is separately theorem-guarded
(C_p-z)u=0 is exactly the recorded weighted Sturm-Liouville deficiency equation
substituting x=6*pi^2*exp(Q)/hbar and d_Q=x*d_x directly into the z=0 raw fiber gives the modified-Bessel equation with order squared -3*p^2/(2*hbar^2)
the p=0 fiber is separately the order-zero modified-Bessel equation with independent I_0 and K_0 reference solutions
for p nonzero the two x^(+/-i*a) zero-energy modes have bounded modulus and both are integrable against the raw weight proportional to x^(1/2) dx at x=0
for p=0 the independent 1 and log(x), equivalently 1 and Q, modes are separately weighted-integrable at x=0
the weighted I asymptotic grows while the weighted K asymptotic is integrable at x=infinity, leaving one square-integrable zero-energy solution
with the global Green-form orientation [W]_-infinity^+infinity, the formal traveling-coordinate contribution is -4*i*hbar^2*k*(Abar*A-Bbar*B); its overall sign leaves B=exp(i*theta)A Lagrangian
with the global Green-form orientation, the p=0 affine-coordinate contribution is -2*hbar^2*(Abar*B-Bbar*A); its overall sign leaves B=lambda*A with real projective lambda Lagrangian
theta=0 and theta=pi give distinct fiber boundary lines, so the differential expression does not canonically select one domain

numerical_calculation.scope: independent finite-sample diagnostics of the exact Bessel reduction only; not a deficiency ODE solve or proof of Weyl classification

numerical_checks.statement: I_(i*a) and K_(i*a) satisfy the transformed zero-energy modified-Bessel equation at all fixed p and x samples
the independent I/K evaluations satisfy W{I_nu,K_nu}=-1/x at all reused p and x samples

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: this constructs one closable symmetric raw-C candidate; it does not prove that the ordering or auxiliary measure is forced by the classical constraint
theorem_guards.hypotheses: f is smooth and strictly positive; C_min=f^(-1)H_hat is declared on C_c^infinity in L2(f dQ dphi), and the integration-by-parts identities are exact

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the closure is decomposable over Lebesgue p with minimal scalar fibers; the executable plane-wave calculation alone is only a symbol check and does not choose fiber extensions
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the coefficients are independent of phi; the phi Fourier transform is unitary; the transformed core contains C_c^infinity(R_Q) tensor Schwartz(R_p), and the formal plane-wave symbol check fixes C_p on that common algebraic core
theorem_guards.theorem: Fourier-Plancherel decomposition of a translation-invariant differential operator and closure of its minimal fibers

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: endpoint type is independent of the nonreal spectral parameter, so the separately audited z=0 Bessel integrability classifies Q=-infinity as limit-circle and Q=+infinity as limit-point
theorem_guards.hypotheses: after multiplying by -1, each real-p fiber has leading coefficient 2*hbar^2>0, weight f>0, real locally integrable potential 72*pi^4*exp(2Q)-3*p^2, and minimal core C_c^infinity(R)
theorem_guards.theorem: Weyl limit-point/limit-circle alternative for real singular Sturm-Liouville expressions

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the minimal scalar fiber has n_plus=n_minus=1 for every p; this is a fiber statement, not the dimension or full extension classification of the two-dimensional operator
theorem_guards.hypotheses: both p nonzero and p=0 have two weighted-integrable local solutions at Q=-infinity and one at Q=+infinity
theorem_guards.theorem: Weyl deficiency-index theorem for one limit-circle and one limit-point endpoint

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the executable traveling/affine Wronskian ledgers fix the oriented asymptotic sign convention, while actual maximal-domain boundary maps are Wronskian limits against a real zero-energy reference pair normalized at a finite Q_0; literal u(-infinity) and u'(-infinity) are not used
theorem_guards.hypotheses: for p nonzero, I_(+/-i*a)(x) is asymptotic to (x/2)^(+/-i*a)/Gamma(1+/-i*a), hence to constant multiples of exp(+/-i*k_p*Q); for p=0, I_0 and K_0 are asymptotic to 1 and -log(x), hence to 1 and an affine Q mode
theorem_guards.theorem: DLMF small-argument modified-Bessel asymptotics plus singular Sturm-Liouville boundary-form theory

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: one real projective, equivalently U(1), boundary line gives a self-adjoint scalar-fiber extension; the exact A/B formulas are asymptotic-coordinate ledgers, not a claim that arbitrary maximal-domain functions have literal plane-wave limits
theorem_guards.hypotheses: for each fixed p choose real zero-energy c_p,s_p with W(c_p,s_p)=1 at Q_0=0; the limit-circle theorem gives Wronskian boundary limits on D(C_p,max), and the global Green form is oriented as [W]_-infinity^+infinity
theorem_guards.theorem: one-limit-circle one-limit-point Sturm-Liouville boundary maps and von Neumann extension theory

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: this audit records only the conditional recipe for a p-preserving decomposable extension and does not construct or promote a measurable global self-adjoint domain; equal fiber indices and Borel theta alone are insufficient
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the Fourier base is Lebesgue p; finite-Q reference solutions depend continuously on p^2, but the limiting boundary maps and chosen extension domains/resolvents must still form a measurable field, in addition to any Borel theta(p)
theorem_guards.theorem: reduction theory for unbounded closed operators and measurable direct integrals

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the audit does not classify general p-mixing extensions, and a p=0 boundary parameter has no full direct-integral effect unless an extra atom is declared
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the full deficiency spaces are infinite-dimensional over p; general unitaries N_plus to N_minus can mix fibers, while the singleton p=0 has zero Lebesgue base measure
theorem_guards.theorem: von Neumann deficiency-space and direct-integral scope separation

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the fixed-p extension debt proves that extra quantum data are required and kills automatic C-to-H equivalence; it neither proves inequivalence of every extension nor supplies a measurable global extension, endpoint transform, BFV, physics, or TOE result
theorem_guards.hypotheses: no extension theta(p), raw-C spectral resolution, zero-fiber group average, rigging map, physical product, or domain-preserving observable intertwiner is computed
